summary: The bill amends federal mining law to let operators locate multiple 5-acre mill sites on public land for waste rock, tailings, and related operations under an approved plan, and directs claim-maintenance fees from those sites into a new Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund used to clean up old mines.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes the Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund but funds it solely through redirection of existing claim maintenance fees with no new appropriations authorized. It does not expand or reduce overall government spending levels.
The bill references and slightly restructures collection of existing claim maintenance and location fees for mill sites but does not alter tax rates, create new taxes, or change tax policy.
No provisions relate to healthcare, insurance, or medical services.
No provisions relate to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions relate to reproductive health or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense spending.

The bill facilitates additional mill sites for hardrock mining operations on public lands. While it includes explicit savings clauses preserving all existing environmental statutes, the core purpose is to reduce regulatory barriers to mining activities, producing a modest pro-development effect.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety-net benefits.

The bill creates no new spending authority or revenue changes that would materially affect deficits or the national debt.
